dedupe_keys.name: ev charging impact co simulation framework on distribution feeders opendss with smart ds san francisco feeders and qgis

description: This record describes a co-simulation framework, published as an arXiv preprint in May 2025 by researchers at California State University Northridge, for analysing the impact of large-scale electric vehicle charging on power distribution networks that are already near capacity. The framework builds a detailed, scalable model of the distribution system in the open-source simulator OpenDSS, using high-fidelity synthetic data from the SMART-DS project for three feeders of an urban substation in San Francisco, modelled down to the household level. It adds QGIS geospatial visualisation to show where extra charging load stresses the grid, and integrates projected load profiles derived from U.S. Department of Energy data covering vehicle types, usage patterns, charging behaviour and adoption rates. Scenarios range from light to heavy charging and compare distributed with centralised charging patterns; the structure is modular so it can be adapted to other locations, feeders and adoption rates. Access: the paper is open access, licensed CC BY 4.0 on the arXiv page; the abstract does not point to released code. Caveats: results rest on synthetic feeders and projected profiles, not measured utility data. It suits distribution capacity planning for EV adoption, and relates to the SMART-DS synthetic distribution models catalogued here.
